title: New Uniswap V3 positions may only be minted inside governance-set tick bounds aligned to the pool's tick spacing
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.9.2.5 branches on a sentinel: when `tokenId` is zero the operator mints a new position "after checking the requested `tick` range is within the governance-set bounds and aligned to the pool's tick spacing"; otherwise the operator "must increase liquidity on the existing position owned by the `proxy`".

Both halves constrain the relayer. Minting is the only path that can create a new price range, and it is bounded by parameters governance sets — so the relayer chooses *where within* an approved band to concentrate liquidity, not which bands Grove is willing to hold. Increasing is restricted to positions the proxy already owns, so a relayer cannot direct Grove capital into a third party's NFT position.

Tick-spacing alignment is not cosmetic: Uniswap V3 only permits initialisable ticks at multiples of the pool's spacing, so an unaligned range would revert deeper in the call stack with a less legible error. Checking at Grove's boundary converts an external failure into a local, named one.

The consequence for concentrated liquidity risk is that the set of ranges Grove can ever occupy is enumerable from governance configuration alone, without inspecting the relayer's transaction history.
description: tokenId = 0 selects mint, and only then is the tick range checked; a non-zero tokenId may only add to a position already owned by the proxy, so relayers cannot create arbitrary ranges.
